findings.text: Timekeeping notification provides single switchpoint for changing the monotonic reference source. Contract is idempotent when the requested source is already active. Otherwise the observable outcome is that accelerated reads are consistent with the final active source capability, tick handling has observed any change, and status distinguishes landed versus not landed.

Sleep interface offers millisecond blocking plus tick based blocking in interruptible and uninterruptible variants. Contract guarantees the caller remains blocked until expiry or, for the interruptible variant, an interrupting event, with tick granularity and correct remaining time reporting.

Timer interface allows arming for a stored expiry, synchronous cancellation that also waits for an in-flight handler, and release of on-stack tracking. Arming is defined only for non pending timers. Synchronous cancellation reports prior pending state.

Supervision interface allows declaring a source unstable with idempotent marker semantics. Effect includes loss of high resolution eligibility and watchdog eligibility, plus asynchronous reassessment when the source is registered and boot has completed.

Eligibility for best selection requires boot completion and non empty ordering, exclusion of test sources, optional exclusion of the current source, and, during one-shot tick operation, restriction to high resolution capable sources. Result is the highest rated eligible entry.

Override name, when non empty and matching a non test listed source, supersedes rating order subject to one-shot compatibility. Incompatible unstable overrides are discarded with diagnostic, while unverified incompatible overrides remain pending for later validation without immediate adoption.
List order invariant is non increasing rating from head to tail. Insertion and rating change preserve this order by splicing at the first lower rated position.

Unstable marker is monotonic within the observed fragments: once set it is not cleared here. Associated invariant is that unstable sources carry neither high resolution suitability nor watchdog eligibility. Unregistered sources converge to zero rating.
Masked cycle difference beyond a caller supplied plausibility bound is treated as zero. This prevents backward time steps from corrupting accumulation.

Nanosecond conversion is bounded by the source advertised cycle limit: deltas within the limit use the standard scaling path while larger deltas use a wider safe path. Both paths start from the same masked bounded delta.

Multiplier and shift pair maximizes accuracy under a worst case interval constraint derived from caller supplied maximum seconds and rates. Larger shifts are preferred while still fitting the constrained range.

Infinite timeout never arms a timer and simply schedules. Negative timeout is a caller error that is diagnosed and yields zero remaining with runnable state restored. Finite non negative timeout yields remaining ticks clamped at zero.

Modification may complete without wheel movement when the requested expiry matches the stored one, or when a reduce-only request would not advance expiry, or when the wheel position for the new expiry coincides with the current position. Reduce-only never moves expiry later.

Association invariant is that a queued timer belongs to the base matching its CPU and pinned or deferrable attributes. Reassociation across bases preserves pending semantics via a migrating marker and is forbidden while the same timer is executing.

Synchronous deletion is linearizable with handler execution: it either detaches a non running timer or waits for completion and retries. Shutdown additionally establishes handler cleared as terminal state under lock.

Base assignment is a pure function of timer attributes and build configuration: pinned selects local, otherwise global, with deferrable diverted to a dedicated base when common no-hz support is present.
Sequence wait terminates on three disjoint conditions: peer error recorded, local timeout budget exceeded, or sequence reaching its cap. Only sequences below the cap count as successful handover.

Self test sampling succeeds exactly when observed flag combination matches expectation before the call budget expires and without stop request. Unexpected unstable or high resolution markers cause immediate failure; absence of expected markers at budget exhaustion causes timeout failure unless no marker was expected.

Suite acceptance requires sequential acceptance of four injection scenarios with fixed budgets: clean operation expecting high resolution readiness, delay expecting no marker, and positive plus negative injections expecting instability. Any scenario failure fails the whole suite.
Marking unstable and linking into watchdog supervision are atomic under a dedicated interrupt saving spinlock. The idempotence test and the mutation share the same critical section.

All decisions about pending state, shutdown state, base time forwarding, and enqueue or detach occur while holding the relevant base lock with interrupts saved. Cross base movement uses an ordered release and acquire pair with a migrating marker bridging the gap.

First error wins for remote coordination results under a global raw lock with scoped acquisition. Concurrent setters do not overwrite the initial outcome but still advance sequencing to release peers.

Completion waiting for ordinary timers coordinates with expiry execution through a waiter count and a bottom-half exclusion lock held across callbacks. The counting ensures the waiter observes handler termination without blocking further expiries.

Per-CPU coordination record colocates call control, progress tracking, outcome storage, dual timestamp slots, source reference, isolated sequence counter, and timeout budget. Call control is placed first for alignment and the sequence counter is isolated to reduce cache interference.

Global exchange record combines mutual exclusion with outcome storage, sequence progress, separate reference and tested accumulations, dual timestamps, and current driver CPU identity. The whole record is cache line isolated for concurrent cross-CPU use.

Outcome vocabulary separates success from frequency assessment failures and from remote coordination failures. Frequency group covers absent reference, readout timeout, reset requirement, and skew. Coordination group covers peer timeout and peer skew.

Skew assessment alternates publishing and validating phases synchronized by monotonic sequence increments. Each participant publishes locally before observing remotely to limit coherence cost. Oversized masked delta or budget expiry moves the exchange to a terminal failure outcome.

Timer states comprise idle, pending, running, and migrating, with handler cleared as absorbing shutdown. Transitions among the first four occur only under base lock. Synchronous deletion distinguishes running from non running to choose between waiting and detaching.

Override handling has stable outcomes of adopted, discarded, or deferred. Adoption requires compatibility with active tick mode. Discard applies to proven incompatibility with instability. Deferral preserves the request for future watchdog validation.

Self test lifecycle starts at init with creation of a named thread, proceeds through registration, sequential suite execution in two locality modes, deregistration, and then either termination or long idle sleep for modular builds. Cleanup requests thread termination when the thread exists.
Asynchronous reassessment after instability is initiated through a work item whose sole effect is to launch a transient thread for final selection. The work item itself never performs selection.

Selection finalization requires a rendezvous that is forbidden from workqueue context due to hotplug ordering. Attempting it there would deadlock. The design therefore delegates to a separate thread, with missed launches recovered by later scans.

Synchronous deletion in hard interrupt context is safe only for interrupt safe timers. On real-time preemptible builds, deletion of ordinary timers also requires preemption enabled due to sleeping wait. Violations risk deadlock.
Re-arming a pending timer through the simple arm operation is a caller error that is warned once and ignored. Correct adjustment of pending timers uses modification operations.
Supervision timing uses a half tick period together with a fifty microsecond ceiling for readout and for default remote waiting. These bounds limit validation latency.

Remote waiting budget grows with interconnect distance from a per-distance quantum derived from the default timeout, capped at five hundred microseconds. This balances tolerance for distant CPUs against bounded detection time.
Frequency tolerance encodings use shift values eleven and eight to represent tighter versus looser parts per million allowances. Tighter tolerance corresponds to larger shift.
Validation effort is bounded by three frequency retries and by a ten step cross-CPU sequence limit. The sequence limit doubles as a sentinel that forces wait exit.

Fast read availability after notification is enabled exactly when the final active source equals the requested source and advertises inline capability. Builds without inline support model both toggles as no-ops with identical observable outcome.
Cleared handler denotes shutdown and forbids further queueing. The test is performed under base lock to synchronize with concurrent shutdown.
Liveness of a dispatched cross-CPU check can be tested non destructively by inspecting the lock marker of its call descriptor. No acquisition is required for the probe.

Selection and supervision state resides in file scoped storage for current, suspend and watchdog references, watchdog timer, override name, boot completion, suspend stamp, running marker and pending reset count, with mutex and spinlock serialization available.
Diagnostics from clocksource handling share a common module name prefix applied through a format wrapper.
One build variant defines completion waiting as a no-op, indicating that expiry synchronization is provided by other means in that configuration.
